title: Constructibility of the exceptional system limit
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with compactification $c$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Fix reduction/limit calculi $S_X,S_Z,S_Y$ and any finite-operation realization $r$ on normalized coefficient systems with constructible finite-Tor levels [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, def-sf-finite-adjunction-diagram-data, def-coef-finite-adjunction-system-data]. Write $\mathcal E_r$ for its system exceptional functor, $\mathcal R_Y$ for reduction, and $\mathcal L_X$ for total derived limit. If $L\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], then $\mathcal L_X\mathcal E_r\mathcal R_YL$ belongs to $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Only this objectwise preservation is asserted; no integral adjunction or compact-support comparison is asserted.

source.place: Accepted specified-adjunction interface, exists_unique docstring: right preservation from duality and common Tor bounds (paragraph 1).

proof.text: Apply sfFiniteOperations_intrinsicExceptionalBounds of lem-sf-finite-intrinsic-exceptional-bounds once to f and c. It gives integers cMinus,cPlus independent of E and the positive coefficient exponent. For L use its common input reduction interval [a,b]. Reduction_domain puts each evaluated reduction in the finite-Tor domain; reductionEvaluation transports that membership to the actual scalar reduction. Apply the uniform interval assertion to these inputs. Uniqueness of the ordinary etale right adjoint at c compares the finite exceptional functor used by FiniteExceptional.G with sfFiniteOperationsIntrinsicRight, after the same intrinsic-coordinate conjugation.

The exceptional output system is normalized. Unrestricted actual normalized reconstruction makes its total limit complete and its system counit invertible. Convert completeness to the intrinsic convention. For each n compose inverse reductionEvaluation at the limit, evaluation of the actual exceptional counit, exceptionalEvaluation, the finite exceptional functor on input reductionEvaluation, and the right-adjoint comparison from step 1. This identifies the actual reduction of the limit with the uniformly bounded finite exceptional output.

Transfer finite constructibility along these isomorphisms using isomorphism closure of bounded constructible objects. Homology of each isomorphism transfers its cohomological support bound [a+cMinus,b+cPlus]. Enlarge this possibly unordered interval to [min(a+cMinus,b+cPlus),max(a+cMinus,b+cPlus)] so that the required endpoints are ordered even for zero objects and empty schemes. Together with completeness these are the two clauses of sfIntegralConstructible. No uniform bound on the entire system category is asserted.

proof_origin.place: Accepted interface exceptional preservation, using the existing coefficient-independent intrinsic exceptional bounds rather than auxiliary absolute system-duality choices.
